title: Cache Hit-Rate Dashboards — Wireframes (early outline)
body:
Context
- Purpose: early mock outline for cache efficiency dashboards (prefix cache + KV cache) to support SRE + Runtime triage during regressions.
- This is NOT final panel naming. It’s a wireframe: what pages exist, what’s at top, and how we expect people to navigate.
- Primary use case: “cache hit-rate dipped” or “unit cost spiked” and oncall needs to quickly answer:
  1) Is this real or telemetry missing?
  2) Where is it happening (model/route/region/deployment mode)?
  3) Why (miss reason, eviction pressure, version mismatch, policy changes, request shape shift)?
  4) What can we do now (rollback, routing, knobs, disable caching on a route, increase cache bytes, reduce churn)?

Operating assumptions (for wireframe)
- Breakdowns we care about: model, model_version, route, deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region, request shape (prompt length buckets), and miss_reason.
- Cardinality guardrails are mandatory (no arbitrary tenant_id; route must be allowlisted; top-N lists instead of full dimensions).
- We should avoid “free-form” drilldowns that accidentally create 100k series.

Global filter bar (present on every dashboard page)
- Time range: last 30m / 6h / 24h / 7d (default 6h)
- Environment: prod / canary / staging (default prod)
- Deployment mode: Hosted / Dedicated / Private / All (default All)
- Region: us-east-1 / us-west-2 / eu-west-1 / … / All (default All)
- Model family (curated): e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen, etc. (default All)
- Model (curated allowlist): model_id (default All)
- Model version: model_version_id (optional; default All)
- Route (allowlisted): route_id or route_name (optional; default All)
- Prompt length bucket: p0–pN buckets (optional; default All)

Optional “safe” filters / toggles
- Show only “top N routes by traffic” toggle (default ON) with N=20
- Compare to previous period toggle (default OFF)
- Show “SLO guardrail thresholds” overlay toggle (default ON for SRE views)

NOT in filter bar (intentionally)
- Tenant/customer identifier (unless we have a curated tier label or internal-only hash w/ strict sampling; TBD)
- Raw prompt signatures (never)

Dashboard IA (tabs/pages)
1) Overview (one page to answer: where + how bad + whether telemetry is healthy)
2) Miss reasons (why misses are happening)
3) Eviction & pressure (cache memory pressure, evictions, churn)
4) Wasted prefill (cost signal / ineffective prefill)
5) Telemetry health (pipeline + cardinality drop detection; should be boring but crucial)

PAGE 1 — OVERVIEW (wireframe)
Top row: “Are we worse?”
A1. Cache hit-rate (time series)
- Two lines: prefix cache hit-rate, KV cache hit-rate (definitions per ADR)
- Breakdown: none by default; optional split by deployment mode (toggle)
- Annotation markers: runtime release deploys + config flag changes + model rollout events (if available)

A2. Traffic context (small multiples)
- Requests/sec OR tokens/sec (prefill + decode) time series
- Prompt tokens distribution (stacked by prompt-length bucket) — to catch workload mix changes

A3. Cost proxy / efficiency (time series)
- Wasted prefill tokens rate (tokens/sec) and wasted prefill ratio
- (Optional) “prefill compute time wasted” if we have it; otherwise tokens only

Second row: “Where is it happening?”
B1. Hit-rate by region (bar)
- Bars: prefix hit-rate, KV hit-rate (side-by-side)
- Sorted ascending (worst first)
- Click a region to set global filter

B2. Hit-rate by model (table)
- Columns: model_id, prefix_hit_rate, kv_hit_rate, wasted_prefill_ratio, req/s (or tokens/s)
- Sorted by impact: (req/s * delta hit-rate) heuristic (approx for wireframe)
- Click row to drill into model

B3. Hit-rate by route (table, top N)
- Same columns as B2 + miss_reason_top (most common)
- Requires route allowlist (otherwise empty / “not enabled”)

Third row: “Is it memory pressure or correctness?”
C1. Evictions/sec (time series)
- Split by eviction reason (if available; otherwise total)
- Overlay with hit-rate dip

C2. Cache memory pressure (gauges)
- Current prefix_cache_bytes used / limit
- KV cache pressure indicator (e.g., utilization, admission failures)
- NOTE: make clear these are per-runtime aggregate; avoid per-node unless we have a separate infra dashboard

C3. Miss reasons (stacked area, top 5)
- miss_reason: capacity, ttl_expired, policy_disabled, hash_mismatch, version_mismatch, other
- This is a “preview”; full drilldown is Page 2

Footer callouts (SRE quick actions)
- Link: Runbook “Cache regressions triage” (TBD final location)
- Link: “Telemetry health” page
- Link: “Recent changes” (deploys/config) page if exists; otherwise annotate in charts

PAGE 2 — MISS REASONS (wireframe)
Goal: confirm whether the dip is expected (workload shift) vs bug/config vs capacity.

Panels
D1. Miss reason distribution over time (stacked area)
- Default: top 5 reasons + other
- Expectation: capacity spikes correlate with eviction/pressure; version_mismatch correlates with rollouts; policy_disabled correlates with route toggles

D2. Miss reason by model (heatmap)
- Rows: model_id, columns: miss_reason, cell: miss_ratio
- Click row = drill into model filter

D3. Miss reason by route (table top N)
- Columns: route, miss_reason, miss_ratio, hit_rate, wasted_prefill_ratio, traffic
- Provide “only show routes with traffic > X” guard

D4. Version mismatch breakdown (if reason exists)
- Time series: version_mismatch misses
- Table: model_version_id pairs (requested vs cached?) — TBD feasibility; may be too cardinality heavy
- Note: if we can’t do pairs safely, show just counts and correlate with rollout timeline

D5. Hash mismatch / canonicalization hint panel
- If hash_mismatch exists: show trend + prompt-length bucket correlation
- Note: might indicate prompt canonicalization not applied for streaming chat or tool call fields changing; add a text hint panel with common causes

PAGE 3 — EVICTION & PRESSURE (wireframe)
Goal: determine if we’re failing due to memory pressure or overly aggressive TTL/admission.

Panels
E1. Evictions/sec by reason (stacked)
- Reasons: capacity, ttl, manual, compaction, unknown (whatever taxonomy ships)

E2. Cache utilization vs limit (time series)
- prefix_cache_bytes_used / prefix_cache_bytes_limit
- KV cache equivalent (if there is a clean metric)

E3. Admission failures / cache bypasses (time series)
- count of “not admitted due to policy/size/capacity”
- NOTE: may overlap with miss_reason; keep consistent semantics

E4. Prompt-length bucket vs eviction correlation (scatter or dual chart)
- X: prompt length bucket
- Y: eviction rate or capacity miss ratio
- Intended to show long prompts crowding out cache

E5. Top routes by eviction impact (table)
- columns: route, evictions/sec, capacity_miss_ratio, wasted_prefill_ratio, traffic

PAGE 4 — WASTED PREFILL (wireframe)
Goal: quantify cost bleed and identify where caching isn’t helping (especially chat/streaming).

Panels
F1. Wasted prefill tokens ratio (time series)
- With compare-to-previous-period toggle to see regression

F2. Wasted prefill by route (table top N)
- columns: route, wasted_prefill_ratio, prefill_tokens/sec, hit_rate, miss_reason_top
- add quick hint text: “High wasted prefill + high hash_mismatch often means prompt canonicalization drift.”

F3. Wasted prefill by prompt-length bucket (bar)
- show if mostly from long prompts

F4. Wasted prefill vs latency (dual axis)
- p95 latency vs wasted prefill ratio to detect if we’re paying extra AND slower

F5. Streaming retry marker panel (if available)
- If retries were double-counting before, add a panel to detect spikes in retry events correlated with wasted prefill
- NOTE: if this is trace-only, we may just link to trace search recipe

PAGE 5 — TELEMETRY HEALTH (wireframe)
Goal: avoid false incidents caused by missing metrics, label drops, or sampling misconfig.

Panels
G1. Metric ingest volume (time series)
- per metric group: hit/miss counters, eviction counters, wasted prefill
- Expect stable-ish with traffic

G2. Label drop / cardinality guard counters (time series)
- ingestion_dropped_series_count
- ingestion_dropped_samples_count
- breakdown by drop_reason (forbidden_label, over_budget, invalid_tag)

G3. Sampling rate visibility (table)
- Current sampling config by environment (prod/canary)
- If we can’t reliably expose, add “config last changed” annotation

G4. “Zero hits” detector panel
- Percent of routes/models with hit_rate=0 while traffic>threshold
- This catches the SUP-3927 class issue early

G5. Cross-signal consistency checks (simple ratios)
- Example: misses + hits ~= eligible_requests (within tolerance)
- Example: prefix reuse tokens <= prefill tokens

Drilldown interactions (notes)
- Clickable elements should set the global filters (region/model/route) rather than spawning new high-cardinality breakdowns.
- For tables, show only top N by traffic or impact; allow changing N but cap at 50.
- Provide “copy link with filters” button for incident sharing.

Triage flow (how SRE expects to use it)
1) Start on Overview
- Confirm hit-rate dip is real and not a telemetry outage (check Telemetry Health signals quickly)
- Look at prompt-length bucket distribution for workload shift

2) Identify blast radius
- Which region? which model? which route(s)?
- If Dedicated customer incident: filter deployment mode=Dedicated, region, route allowlisted for that customer (if applicable)

3) Determine cause bucket
- Miss reasons page: is it capacity/ttl/policy/version mismatch/hash mismatch?
- Eviction page: pressure/evictions trending up?

4) Immediate mitigation suggestions (for oncall)
- If version_mismatch spike: check recent model rollout; consider rollback or ensure consistent model_version pinning between routes
- If capacity/evictions: consider increasing cache bytes, tightening admission on long prompts, or routing for locality (reduce cross-region churn)
- If policy_disabled: verify per-route caching config + feature flags
- If hash_mismatch: look for prompt canonicalization drift (streaming chat/tool-call fields); coordinate with app team / gateway canonicalization

Open questions / TODOs (wireframe stage)
- Confirm final metric names and exact definitions (hit vs partial hit) from ADR and runtime instrumentation.
- Do we have a stable “route_name” label that is safe to display? If not, only route_id with a lookup table.
- Model version joinability: do we have a single canonical model_version_id in gateway + runtime metrics? (Ethan to confirm)
- Event annotations for rollouts/config changes: what’s the source of truth and can we feed it to dashboards?
- Decide if we need a separate “Dedicated customer view” dashboard pack (tighter permissions and route allowlist).

Notes on presentation / UX (rough)
- Use consistent language: “Prefix cache” vs “KV cache” (no ‘context cache’ synonyms).
- Put a small definition tooltip on every top-level metric (hit-rate, wasted prefill, miss reason taxonomy).
- For any panel where data may be sampled: show a subtle “sampled” badge + current sampling rate.

Change log
- 2025-02-26: initial outline created (Allison)
- 2025-03-02: added Telemetry Health page after label-drop incident discussion (Allison/Sergio)
- 2025-03-08: added triage flow notes + miss reason preview panels (Aisha feedback)
